## warpt.orchestrator

### `parse_arguments` { #orchestrator--parse-arguments }

`parse_arguments()` — `warpt/orchestrator.py`, line 67

Define and parse the WARP command-line interface.

The options that select the run mode and the force engine:

* ``-mode`` (required; ``vc-relax`` or ``preconditioning``): ``vc-relax`` runs the
  preconditioning schedule in ``iter_0`` and then position and lattice steps per
  ``iter_<n>``; ``preconditioning`` runs the force-constant bootstrap only, in
  ``preconditioning/`` under the working directory.
* ``-c`` / ``--calculator`` (``QE``, ``MLIP`` or ``VASP``, default ``QE``): ``QE``
  runs the ``--pwx`` command per sample; ``MLIP`` runs
  ``python3 -m warpt.MLIP_interface --engine <-mle> --device <-mld> --ml_params <-mlp>``
  (+ ``--variant <-mlv>``, ``--conservative`` with ``-mlc``); ``VASP`` runs
  ``python3 -m warpt.VASP_interface --template <--vasp_template>`` with the
  command given by ``--vasp_cmd``.
* ``-mle`` / ``--ml_engine`` (``upet`` or ``mace``, default ``upet``): forwarded as
  ``--engine`` to ``warpt.MLIP_interface``; used only with ``--calculator MLIP``.
* ``-mld`` / ``--ml_device`` (``cpu`` or ``cuda``, default ``cpu``): forwarded as
  ``--device`` to ``warpt.MLIP_interface``; used only with ``--calculator MLIP``.

**Returns**

- `argparse.Namespace` — The parsed CLI options (calculator, structure/master deck, temperature, FC cutoffs, supercell, target stress, schedule, etc.).

**Raises**

- `SystemExit` — With code 2 from argparse on an invalid or missing required option. ``--help`` prints the option list and exits with code 0 (``main`` has printed ``BANNER`` before the arguments are parsed, so the banner appears once).

### `_select_pw_command` { #orchestrator---select-pw-command }

`_select_pw_command(args) -> str` — `warpt/orchestrator.py`, line 346

Return the calculator command string stored as ``ctx.pwscf_run``.

``QE``: ``args.pwx`` or ``"mpirun -n 6 pw.x"``. ``MLIP``:
``python3 -m warpt.MLIP_interface --engine E --device D --ml_params P``, plus
``--variant V`` when ``--ml_variant`` is given and ``--conservative`` when
``--ml_conservative`` is set. ``P`` is made absolute because the samples run in
per-geometry subdirectories. ``VASP``: ``python3 -m warpt.VASP_interface
--template T`` with ``T`` made absolute likewise, the VASP command exported as
``WARPT_VASP_CMD`` and ``MAX_CONC`` defaulting to 1. Calls
`warpt.utilities.die` (exit 1) when ``--ml_params`` is missing for ``MLIP``
or ``--vasp_template`` or ``--vasp_cmd`` is missing for ``VASP``.

### `_parse_sigma_ext` { #orchestrator---parse-sigma-ext }

`_parse_sigma_ext(press_ext)` — `warpt/orchestrator.py`, line 390

Convert ``--press_ext`` into a tension-positive Voigt external stress.

Input values are compression-positive pressures in GPa. One value gives the
hydrostatic target ``[-P, -P, -P, 0, 0, 0]`` (mode ``"scalar"``); three give
the negated diagonal (``"diag3"``); six give the negated Voigt vector
(``"full6"``).

**Parameters**

- **press_ext** (`list[float]`) — One, three or six values in GPa.

**Returns**

- `tuple[str, numpy.ndarray]` — ``(sigma_mode, sigma_ext)``; ``sigma_ext`` is a length-6 Voigt vector in GPa.

**Raises**

Calls `warpt.utilities.die` (exit 1) when ``press_ext`` is None or has a number
of values other than 1, 3 or 6.

### `build_ctx_state` { #orchestrator--build-ctx-state }

`build_ctx_state(args)` — `warpt/orchestrator.py`, line 435

Build the frozen `WarpContext` and the initial `WarpState`.

The working directory becomes ``ctx.root``; ``-m`` and ``-ucp`` are joined to
it (the unit-cell file is read here only for ``--calculator VASP`` and is not
otherwise checked for existence). Picks ``mawk`` when it is on PATH, else ``awk``
(the choice is printed as a ``WARNING: Using ...`` line), selects the calculator
command, parses the supercell flags and the external stress, splits
``--precond_schedule`` at commas into integers (empty entries skipped; ``None``
when the option is absent), and bundles the physical constants used by
`warpt.phonon_stress`. For ``--calculator VASP`` the template directory is
checked against the elements of the unit cell
(`warpt.VASP_interface.check_template`); each warning it returns is printed
as a WARNING line, followed by a ``[warpt] VASP:`` line with the template, the
command and ``MAX_CONC``.

**Parameters**

- **args** (`argparse.Namespace`) — Output of `parse_arguments`.

**Returns**

tuple[WarpContext, WarpState]

**Raises**

Calls `warpt.utilities.die` (exit 1) when the master deck does not
exist, ``--press_ext`` is absent, ``--ml_params`` is missing for ``--calculator MLIP``, ``--vasp_template``
or ``--vasp_cmd`` is missing for ``--calculator VASP``, the VASP template check
fails (an unreadable unit cell included), ``--press_ext`` has a count other
than 1, 3 or 6, or ``--supercell`` has a count other than 1, 3 or 9.
``ValueError`` from ``int()`` on a non-integer ``--precond_schedule`` or
``--supercell`` entry.

### `main` { #orchestrator--main }

`main()` — `warpt/orchestrator.py`, line 574

Entry point: print the banner, parse arguments, build the context, then run
``run_vc_relax`` (after printing the resume plan) or ``run_preconditioning``
according to ``-mode``.

## warpt.workflow_preconditioning

### `parse_cv_r2` { #workflow-preconditioning--parse-cv-r2 }

`parse_cv_r2(logpath='extract_forceconstants.log')` — `warpt/workflow_preconditioning.py`, line 51

Parse the cross-validation R^2 values from an ``extract_forceconstants`` log.

Scans for the first line containing ``cross-validation`` and takes the third token of the
first following ``second order:`` and ``third order:`` lines; once the second-order value
has been read, the scan stops at the next line starting with ``rms`` or, in any letter
case, ``forces``.

**Parameters**

- **logpath** (`str`) — Log file (default ``extract_forceconstants.log``).

**Returns**

- `tuple[float or None, float or None]` — ``(r2_second, r2_third)``; ``None`` for a value not found or when the file is missing.

### `save_local_samples_snapshot` { #workflow-preconditioning--save-local-samples-snapshot }

`save_local_samples_snapshot(geom_dir)` — `warpt/workflow_preconditioning.py`, line 137

Copy this geom's TDEP inputs into a ``local_samples/`` snapshot.

Copies the geom's ``infile.{positions,forces,stat,meta}`` into ``local_samples/``.
`run_preconditioning` calls it before `warpt.tdep_collect.combine_samples`
appends the previous geom's rows to those files, so the next geom can reuse this geom's
own samples.

**Parameters**

- **geom_dir** (`str`) — The preconditioning geometry directory.

### `run_preconditioning` { #workflow-preconditioning--run-preconditioning }

`run_preconditioning(ctx, state)` — `warpt/workflow_preconditioning.py`, line 159

Run the preconditioning schedule under ``preconditioning/`` in the current directory.

For each sample count ``ns`` in the schedule (``ctx.precond_schedule`` or the default
``[8, 32, 32, 48, 48, 64, 64]``) a directory ``geom_<k>`` is created and, unless it is
already complete, sampled with ``ns`` configurations, combined with the previous geom's
``local_samples/`` (k >= 1), fitted with ``extract_forceconstants`` (FC2 + FC3; the
first-order structure update is added from geom_2 on when the previous geom's minimum
frequency exceeds ``ctx.firstorder_min_freq`` THz), followed by ``ifc_pressure`` and a DOS
dispersion on the first valid q-grid of 22^3, 20^3, 18^3, 16^3, 14^3. From geom_1 on the
geom is gated: minimum frequency > -1e-5 THz and second-order cross-validation
R^2 >= ``CV_R2_MIN``; the first geom that passes ends the schedule. An already-complete
geom (resume) is re-gated instead of recomputed.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — Run configuration (``ucp``, ``sc_opts``, ``precond_schedule``, ``firstorder_min_freq``).
- **state** (`context_state.WarpState`) — Mutable run state; ``use_fake_fc`` is set to True for geom_0 and False for every later geom that is computed.

**Returns**

- `str` — Absolute path of the geom directory that passed the gate; the process is left in that directory. The one exception is a one-element schedule whose geom_0 is already complete: that directory is returned, but the process is left in ``preconditioning/``.

**Side effects**

Creates ``preconditioning/`` and the ``geom_<k>`` directories and writes the files listed
in the module docstring. Exits via `warpt.utilities.die` when ``ifc_pressure``
fails, when no q-grid yields a valid dispersion (geom_1 on), or when the last geom of the
schedule fails the gate (geom_0 is never gated, so a one-element schedule always exits
here on a fresh run).

## warpt.workflow_vc_relax

### `_symmetry_ops` { #workflow-vc-relax---symmetry-ops }

`_symmetry_ops(path, symprec=1e-05)` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 53

Canonical set of symmetry operations of a POSCAR, expressed in its own cell basis.

Each operation is ``(rotation, translation mod 1)``. Translations are reduced
modulo the lattice and rounded, with the 0.99999 -> 0.0 wrap handled explicitly:
without that, numerically identical operations compare as different and the
caller sees a spurious symmetry "loss".

Returns ``None`` if the structure cannot be read or spglib finds nothing, so
callers can skip the check rather than crash.

The returned set depends on both the basis and the origin, so it is only comparable
between structures that share a cell and an origin; see the guard in
`refine_new_lattice`.

Move the content of ``cwd`` into ``fc3_gate_attempt_<attempt + 1>/``.

Every entry except existing ``fc3_gate_attempt_*`` directories is moved. Prints one
``[fc3-gate]`` line and returns the archive path.

`_fc3_gate_restore(attempt: int, cwd: str = '.') -> None` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 113

### `refine_new_lattice` { #workflow-vc-relax--refine-new-lattice }

`refine_new_lattice(ctx, path='outfile.new_vc_ucposcar')` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 134

Restore exact space-group symmetry to the lattice-updated structure in place.

No longer called by the relaxation loop; the two call sites in this module are
commented out and the function is kept for reference. The lattice update applies a
strain projected onto the point group of the current cell
(`warpt.compliance_update.project_strain_onto_point_group`), which keeps the
space group exactly, so this refinement left the updated cell unchanged (changes of
order 1e-15 Å in a P2_1/m test cell). It also does not restore a symmetry that has
been broken: on a cell whose symmetry was broken at the 1e-8 level it returned a cell
of lower symmetry, which the guard below turns into a stop.

Runs ``refine_structure -uc <path> -pf <ctx.ucp>`` (TDEP), which writes
``outfile.refined_cell`` using ``ctx.ucp`` as the symmetry prototype. If the tool exits 0
and that file is non-empty, the symmetry operations of ``path`` and of
``outfile.refined_cell`` are compared (`_symmetry_ops`, when both sets can be
determined): the run is aborted via ``die`` if the original set is not a subset of the
refined set, a ``[refine] SYMMETRY INCREASED`` line is printed if operations were
gained, and ``outfile.refined_cell`` is copied over ``path``. Otherwise a
``[refine][warn]`` line is printed and ``path`` is left unchanged. Returns without
action if ``path`` does not exist.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — ``ctx.ucp``, the initial structure used as the symmetry prototype.
- **path** (`str`) — Structure to refine in place (default ``outfile.new_vc_ucposcar``).

`sigma_ph_converged(ctx, sigma_ph, sigma_ph_prev)` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 226

Element-wise convergence check of the phonon stress between consecutive lattice steps.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — ``press_conv_th`` (GPa) and ``press_conv_noise_k``.

**Returns**

Otherwise ``ok`` is True when every component of ``|sigma_ph - sigma_ph_prev|`` is below its threshold: ``press_conv_th``, or, when ``press_conv_noise_k > 0`` and ``infile.stat`` is readable, per component ``max(press_conv_th, press_conv_noise_k * SE_i)`` with ``SE_i`` from `warpt.noise_gain.stress_standard_error`. ``msg`` lists the component differences in GPa.

### `_ensure_from_stage` { #workflow-vc-relax---ensure-from-stage }

`_ensure_from_stage(ctx, state, stage: str, kind: str)` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 277

Run the stages that `warpt.validity.first_missing_stage` reports missing in the
current directory until it reports none.

``stage`` is accepted and ignored. ``kind`` selects what "complete" means:
``"preconditioning"`` requires the DOS dispersion, ``"lattice"`` requires the Grüneisen
grid and ``outfile.new_vc_ucposcar``, ``"position"`` requires neither; ``ifc_pressure``
output is required for every kind. For ``"lattice"`` the phonons branch calls
`warpt.phonon_stress.internal_stress_voigt`, which deletes
``outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5`` after use, so ``valid_gruneisen()`` stays False and the
loop repeats that branch. Exits via ``die`` when setup files are missing, when a
preconditioning directory still needs sampling, when at the extract stage the geom index
cannot be read from a preconditioning directory's name, when ``ifc_pressure`` fails, when
no q-grid from 30^3 down to 14^3 yields a valid DOS dispersion, when the phonons stage is
requested for a kind other than ``"preconditioning"`` or ``"lattice"``, or when a stage
name is unknown. Not called by `run_vc_relax`, which resumes by its forward walk,
nor by any other module.

### `stress_converged` { #workflow-vc-relax--stress-converged }

`stress_converged(ctx, sigma_int, p_int=None)` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 518

Element-wise convergence check of the internal stress against ``ctx.sigma_ext``.

The target is ``sigma_ext`` in ``scalar`` mode (diagonal ``sigma_ext[0]``, shears

``sigma_int[:3]`` in ``diag3`` mode. Component ``i`` passes when

`warpt.noise_gain.stress_standard_error` (the per-component gate is printed as a
``[convergence]`` line).

- **sigma_int** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Internal stress, Voigt, tension-positive, GPa.
- **p_int** (`float or None`) — Accepted and ignored.

**Returns**

- `tuple[bool, str]` — ``(all compared components pass, message listing the per-component differences in GPa)``.

### `_write_trajectory` { #workflow-vc-relax---write-trajectory }

`_write_trajectory(ctx) -> None` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 608

Run `warpt.get_frames.collect` with the current working directory as root.

``collect`` scans ``iter_0/preconditioning/geom_*``, ``iter_*/position_*`` and
``iter_*/lattice_*`` below that root and writes ``<root>/trajectory.xyz`` when at least
one frame is found, after which one ``[postproc]`` line is printed; with no step
directory below the root nothing is written and nothing is printed. At the call site in
`run_vc_relax` the working directory is the converged ``lattice_`` directory, which
holds no such subdirectory. Every exception is caught and reported as
``[postproc][warn]``. ``ctx`` is unused. The standalone tool,
``python3 -m warpt.get_frames -r <run root>``, must be run on the run root (``ctx.root``).

### `run_vc_relax` { #workflow-vc-relax--run-vc-relax }

`run_vc_relax(ctx, state, resume_plan=None)` — `warpt/workflow_vc_relax.py`, line 631

Drive the variable-cell relaxation for one structure from ``ctx.root``.

Iteration 0 runs `warpt.workflow_preconditioning.run_preconditioning`; every
iteration then runs position steps ``iter_<n>/position_<p>`` (sample ``ctx.num_samples``
configurations, combine with the previous step's samples when its update was below
``ctx.reuse_threshold`` and the lattice did not just change, fit FC2/FC3 with the
first-order structure update, run the DOS dispersion) until the mean and max FC1 are
below ``ctx.fc1_mean_tol`` / ``ctx.fc1_max_tol``, then the lattice step
``iter_<n>/lattice_`` (sample, combine with the last position step's samples when its
update was small and the lattice did not just change, fit, ``ifc_pressure``, phonon
stress ``sigma_ph``, optional FC3 gate, convergence report, symmetry-preserving lattice
update). Converged when the stress gate, the change of ``sigma_ph`` since the
previous lattice step, and the previous lattice step's ``|dV/V| < 0.01`` all pass; then
``final_structure.vasp`` is written and the function returns.

Position directories are checked with `warpt.validity.first_missing_stage` and
skipped when complete; a lattice directory is skipped only when ``final_structure.vasp``
(converged run, the function returns) or ``outfile.new_vc_ucposcar`` exists (its
``|dV/V|`` and ``outfile.sigma_ph`` are re-read), otherwise it is recomputed. A restarted
run therefore walks forward from iteration 0 over the existing tree.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — Run configuration.
- **state** (`context_state.WarpState`) — Mutable run state (``lattice_changed``, ``last_update_significant``, ``fc3_gate_events``; ``last_lattice_rel_change`` and ``prev_sigma_ph`` are added here).
- **resume_plan** (`dict or None`) — Output of `warpt.restart_check.find_resume_plan`; only reported in a ``[restart]`` line.

**Side effects**

Creates the ``iter_<n>`` tree; writes ``outfile.sigma_ph``, ``outfile.new_vc_ucposcar``,
``outfile.fc3_gate`` (gate on),
``fc3_gate_attempt_<k>/`` (on a failed FC3-gate attempt) and ``final_structure.vasp`` in
lattice directories and ``vc_restart.ucposcar`` in ``ctx.root``; prints the timing
summary at the start of every iteration after the first. Exits via ``die`` when
``ifc_pressure`` fails or when the FC3-gate
attempt to be restored is missing.

### `combine_samples` { #tdep-collect--combine-samples }

`combine_samples(prev_dir, current_dir)` — `warpt/tdep_collect.py`, line 242

Append a previous geometry's sampled data onto the current one.

Concatenates ``infile.positions``/``infile.forces``, appends the previous
``infile.stat`` rows with shifted sample indices, updates ``infile.meta``'s
sample count, and refreshes the ``calc_samples`` copy. Two callers:
`warpt.workflow_preconditioning.run_preconditioning` (sliding window,
``prev_dir`` = the previous geometry's ``local_samples/``) and
`warpt.workflow_vc_relax.run_vc_relax`, which merges the previous step's
samples into the current position step or into the lattice step when that step's
structure update was below ``--reuse_threshold`` and the lattice did not just change.

**Parameters**

- **prev_dir** (`str`) — Directory whose samples are appended.
- **current_dir** (`str`) — Directory receiving the combined samples.

Returns None.

**Side effects**

Appends to ``current_dir/infile.positions``, ``infile.forces`` and ``infile.stat``,
rewrites line 2 of ``current_dir/infile.meta`` as ``<total> #SCF_steps`` and
overwrites the four files in ``current_dir/calc_samples/``.

Run ``phonon_dispersion_relations --dumpgrid --gruneisen`` until the grid HDF5 exists.

Tries q-grids 16^3, 14^3, 12^3 and 10^3 in that order and returns as soon as the tool

### `sigma_ph_from_dispersion_h5` { #phonon-stress--sigma-ph-from-dispersion-h5 }

`sigma_ph_from_dispersion_h5(ctx, path='outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5')` — `warpt/phonon_stress.py`, line 184

Phonon stress tensor ``sigma_ph`` (3x3, GPa) from a TDEP grid-dispersion HDF5.

``frequencies`` is taken as angular frequency in rad/s (TDEP's grid dump, unit
'Hz (angular)'), so ``E = ctx.hbar_eVs * frequencies`` is in eV. For every q-point and
mode with ``E > 1e-8`` eV the mode-Grüneisen parameter (tensor if ``gruneisen_tensors``
is present, else scalar ``gruneisen_parameters`` times the identity) is weighted by
``E * (1/2 + n_BE(E, ctx.temp))``; the sum is divided by the number of q-points and by
the cell volume from ``lattice_vectors`` and converted with ``ctx.EV_TO_GPA_A3``. The
result is in the file's compression-positive sense; the caller negates it.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — Provides ``temp`` (K), ``kB_eV``, ``hbar_eVs`` and ``EV_TO_GPA_A3``.
- **path** (`str`) — Grid-dispersion HDF5 (default ``outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5``).

**Returns**

- `numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)` — Phonon stress in GPa.

**Raises**

- `FileNotFoundError` — If ``path`` does not exist.

### `internal_stress_voigt` { #phonon-stress--internal-stress-voigt }

`internal_stress_voigt(ctx, state)` — `warpt/phonon_stress.py`, line 271

Assemble the total internal stress of the current directory for the lattice update.

Reads ``outfile.stress_dft``, ``outfile.stress_fc2`` and ``outfile.stress_fc3`` written by
``ifc_pressure`` (compression-positive; a missing file reads as zeros), negates each and
sums them into ``sigma_res``. If both a second- and a third-order force constant file
are present (``infile.forceconstant``/``outfile.forceconstant`` and the ``_thirdorder``
pair) it runs ``phonon_dispersion_relations --dumpgrid --gruneisen`` on q-grids 16^3,
14^3, 12^3, 10^3 until ``outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5`` appears, computes ``sigma_ph``
from it with `sigma_ph_from_dispersion_h5`, negates it to tension-positive and
deletes the HDF5; otherwise ``sigma_ph`` is zero. Prints a stress diagnostic block.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — Temperature, constants and ``sigma_ext`` (printed).
- **state** (`context_state.WarpState`) — Unused.

**Returns**

- **sigma_res** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6,)`) — ``-(sigma_DFT + sigma_FC2 + sigma_FC3)`` in file sign, i.e. tension-positive, Voigt, GPa.
- **sigma_ph** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6,)`) — Phonon stress, tension-positive, Voigt, GPa.
- **sigma_int** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6,)`) — ``sigma_res + sigma_ph``.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — If no q-grid produces ``outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5``; any exception from the phonon-stress evaluation is re-raised after a ``[WARN]`` line.

### `fc3_ph_mismatch` { #phonon-stress--fc3-ph-mismatch }

`fc3_ph_mismatch(sigma_ph)` — `warpt/phonon_stress.py`, line 368

Mismatch between the real-space and q-space third-order stress.

``sigma_FC3`` (``outfile.stress_fc3``, negated to tension-positive) and ``sigma_ph`` are
the same contraction evaluated in real space and on the q grid, so their sum vanishes up
to q-point interpolation; a large sum indicates an ill-conditioned third-order fit.

**Parameters**

- **sigma_ph** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Phonon stress, Voigt, tension-positive, GPa.

**Returns**

- `tuple[float, numpy.ndarray]` — ``max_i |sigma_FC3,i + sigma_ph,i|`` in GPa and the six-component sum.

### `fc3_gate_verdict` { #phonon-stress--fc3-gate-verdict }

`fc3_gate_verdict(ctx, sigma_ph, attempt, max_retries)` — `warpt/phonon_stress.py`, line 390

Evaluate the optional FC3 / sigma_ph gate for one lattice-step attempt.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — ``fc3_gate_thr`` (GPa, or None for off).

**Returns**

## warpt.compliance_update

### `_read_compliance_tensor` { #compliance-update---read-compliance-tensor }

`_read_compliance_tensor(filename)` — `warpt/compliance_update.py`, line 45

Read a 6x6 Voigt compliance matrix (1/GPa), skipping ``#`` comment lines.

### `read_elastic_constants` { #compliance-update--read-elastic-constants }

`read_elastic_constants(filename, sym_tol=0.001)` — `warpt/compliance_update.py`, line 56

Read and check a user-supplied 6x6 stiffness tensor (GPa) for the lattice update.

The file holds six rows of six numbers, Voigt order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, in the
Cartesian frame of ``infile.ucposcar``; blank lines and lines starting with ``#`` are
skipped. The matrix must be 6x6, symmetric (largest ``|C - C^T|`` relative to the largest
``|C|`` below ``sym_tol``; the symmetrised half-sum is returned) and positive definite,
so that its inverse is a usable compliance. Any violation raises ValueError with the
reason; the orchestrator turns that into a fatal error before the run starts.

**Parameters**

- **filename** (`str`) — Path of the elastic-constants file.
- **sym_tol** (`float`) — Relative asymmetry allowed (default 1e-3).

**Returns**

- **C** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6, 6)`) — Symmetrised stiffness in GPa.

### `project_strain_onto_point_group` { #compliance-update--project-strain-onto-point-group }

`project_strain_onto_point_group(strain_tensor, ucposcar='infile.ucposcar', symprec=1e-05)` — `warpt/compliance_update.py`, line 97

Project a Cartesian strain tensor onto the totally symmetric representation of the point
group of a unit cell.

The strain a crystal can undergo without lowering its symmetry is the subspace invariant
under every point-group operation R (Neumann's principle): ``eps_sym = (1/|G|) sum_R R
eps R^T``, the group average. Applied before the lattice update it keeps, to rounding, the
space group of the current cell; ``||eps - eps_sym||`` is the symmetry-forbidden part,
i.e. the sampling noise of the stress residual. Rows of ``lattice`` are the lattice
vectors, so a Cartesian column vector is ``x_c = A^T x_f``; spglib's rotations act on
fractional vectors, hence ``R_c = A^T R_f (A^T)^-1``. A supergroup's invariant subspace
lies inside the subgroup's, so symmetry raising is not blocked.

**Parameters**

- **strain_tensor** (`array-like, shape (3, 3)`) — Cartesian strain (dimensionless).
- **ucposcar** (`str`) — POSCAR whose point group is used (default ``infile.ucposcar``).
- **symprec** (`float`) — spglib symmetry tolerance in Å (default 1e-5).

**Returns**

- **eps_sym** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)`) — Symmetrised projected strain; the unprojected input if spglib is unavailable or fails.
- **forbidden** (`float`) — Frobenius norm of the projected-out part; ``nan`` when no projection was done.
- **nops** (`int`) — Number of spglib symmetry operations averaged (rotation parts of the space-group operations of ``ucposcar``, repeated once per centring translation of a centred cell); 0 when no projection was done (a ``[lattice][warn]`` line is printed).

### `compliance_update` { #compliance-update--compliance-update }

`compliance_update(ctx, state, sigma_int_voigt, sigma_ext_voigt)` — `warpt/compliance_update.py`, line 157

Compute the strained lattice from the compliance tensor and the stress residual.

Reads ``infile.ucposcar`` and the compliance ``S`` (6x6 Voigt, 1/GPa): the inverse of the
stiffness in ``ctx.elastic_constants`` when that is set (`read_elastic_constants`),
otherwise ``outfile.compliance_tensor``. Forms ``residual = sigma_int - sigma_ext`` and the
damping ``lambda_l``:

* ``lambda_l = ctx.lattice_damping`` (default 1.0);
* if ``ctx.lattice_damping_ladder`` (``'thr:f,thr:f'``, GPa -> factor) is set,
  ``lambda_l`` becomes ``f * ctx.lattice_damping`` for the smallest ``thr`` exceeding
  ``|dsigma|``, where ``|dsigma|`` is ``max_i |residual_i|`` over all six components
  (``scalar``/``full6``) or the three diagonal ones (``diag3``);
* if ``ctx.lattice_noise_z0 > 0``, ``lambda_l`` is multiplied by the gain
  ``z**2/(z**2 + z0**2)`` from `warpt.noise_gain.noise_gain`, with the standard
  errors read from ``infile.stat`` (skipped with a message when that file is missing or
  unreadable, or has fewer than 3 rows or 13 columns).

The engineering Voigt strain ``-lambda_l * S @ residual`` is converted to a tensor
(shears halved), projected onto the point-group-invariant strains of ``infile.ucposcar``
(`project_strain_onto_point_group`) and applied as ``A_new = A (I + eps)``;
components of ``A_new`` below 1e-6 Å in magnitude are set to zero. Prints the damping,
the projection summary and the old and new lattice.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — ``sigma_mode``, ``lattice_damping``, ``lattice_damping_ladder``, ``lattice_noise_z0``, ``elastic_constants``.
- **state** (`context_state.WarpState`) — Unused.
- **sigma_int_voigt, sigma_ext_voigt** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6,)`) — Internal and external stress, Voigt order, tension-positive, GPa.

**Returns**

- **new_lattice** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)`) — Updated lattice vectors (rows), Å.
- **poscar_lines** (`list[str]`) — The lines of ``infile.ucposcar`` for `write_updated_structure`.
- **p_int** (`float`) — ``-(xx + yy + zz)/3`` of ``sigma_int_voigt`` (GPa, compression-positive).

### `write_updated_structure` { #compliance-update--write-updated-structure }

`write_updated_structure(new_lattice, poscar_lines, out_path='outfile.new_vc_ucposcar')` — `warpt/compliance_update.py`, line 296

Write the strained lattice into a POSCAR, keeping the species/coords block.

**Parameters**

- **new_lattice** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)`) — Updated lattice vectors (rows), Å.
- **poscar_lines** (`list[str]`) — Original POSCAR lines (from `compliance_update`).
- **out_path** (`str`) — Output path (default ``outfile.new_vc_ucposcar``).

**Returns**

- `str` — ``out_path``.

`stress_standard_error(stat_path='infile.stat')` — `warpt/noise_gain.py`, line 45

Columns 8-13 (1-based) hold the per-configuration stress in GPa in the order xx, yy, zz,
then three shears (as written by `warpt.tdep_collect.collect_stats`).

**Parameters**

### `noise_z` { #noise-gain--noise-z }

`noise_z(residual_voigt, se6, floor_gpa=1e-06)` — `warpt/noise_gain.py`, line 80

Largest residual-to-noise ratio over the six Voigt components.

Components whose standard error is below ``floor_gpa`` (constant columns,
symmetry-zero shears) use the floor, so a genuinely zero residual gives z = 0
and a finite residual on a noiseless component gives a large z (full step).

**Parameters**

- **residual_voigt** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Stress residual ``sigma_int - sigma_ext``, Voigt order, GPa; only the first six components are used.
- **se6** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Standard errors of the stress components, GPa (`stress_standard_error`).
- **floor_gpa** (`float`) — Lower bound applied to every standard error, GPa (default 1e-6).

**Returns**

- `tuple[float, int]` — ``(z, i_max)``: the largest ``|residual_i| / max(se6_i, floor_gpa)`` and the index of the component that sets it.

### `noise_gain` { #noise-gain--noise-gain }

`noise_gain(residual_voigt, se6, z0)` — `warpt/noise_gain.py`, line 110

Gain ``z**2 / (z**2 + z0**2)`` in [0, 1]; 1.0 when ``z0 <= 0``.

**Parameters**

- **residual_voigt** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Stress residual ``sigma_int - sigma_ext``, Voigt order, GPa.
- **se6** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Standard errors of the stress components, GPa (`stress_standard_error`).
- **z0** (`float`) — Residual-to-noise ratio at which the gain is 1/2 (dimensionless; ``ctx.lattice_noise_z0``).

**Returns**

- `tuple[float, float, int]` — ``(gain, z, i_max)`` with the gain in [0, 1] and ``z``, ``i_max`` from `noise_z` (called with its default floor).

### `noise_floor` { #noise-gain--noise-floor }

`noise_floor(pct, se6, k)` — `warpt/noise_gain.py`, line 137

Convergence threshold raised to ``k * max_i SE_i`` when that exceeds ``pct``.

No pipeline stage calls this function; the per-component floor of the stress gate is
formed in `warpt.workflow_vc_relax.stress_converged` and
`warpt.workflow_vc_relax.sigma_ph_converged`.

**Parameters**

- **pct** (`float`) — Base convergence threshold, GPa.
- **se6** (`array-like, shape (6,)`) — Standard errors of the stress components, GPa; only the first six are used.
- **k** (`float`) — Multiplier of the largest standard error (dimensionless).

**Returns**

- `tuple[float, float]` — ``(max(pct, floor), floor)`` in GPa, with ``floor = k * max_i se6_i``.

### `load_spacegroup` { #wyckoff-projector--load-spacegroup }

`load_spacegroup(spg_number, hall_number=None)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 163

Load the record of ONE setting of a space group from the bundled table.

The table holds every setting of every group (527 records). The record's operators are
applied to the structure as given, without a setting transformation, so the structure is
taken to be in spglib's default setting (origin choice 1 for the 24 two-origin groups;
unique axis b, cell choice 1 for the monoclinic groups), which is not always the ITA
reference setting. The record is selected in this order:

  1. if ``hall_number`` (spglib's) is given, the record with this ``it_number`` whose
     ``spglib_hall_numbers`` contains it;
  2. else the record named by the table index
     ``indicies.index_it_number_to_spglib_default_spacegroups`` (JSON-LD schema only),
     provided its ``it_number`` matches;
  3. else the first record with this ``it_number``.

Per Wyckoff record the JSON-LD schema stores ``orbit`` and ``orbit_mod_centering`` as
lists of ``{matrix, vector, xyz}``; the flat schema stores ``orbit_affine`` /
``orbit_mod_centering_affine`` as 4x4 rational matrices.

**Parameters**

- **spg_number** (`int`) — International Tables space-group number.
- **hall_number** (`int or None`) — spglib Hall number of the setting, if known.

**Returns**

- `dict` — The setting record.

**Raises**

- `KeyError` — If no record has this ``it_number``.

### `build_A` { #wyckoff-projector--build-a }

`build_A(first_orbit_ita)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 320

Build the (3 × n_dof) displacement basis matrix A for the representative
Wyckoff site from its ITA symbolic coordinate string.

A encodes WHICH fractional directions the representative is free to move:
each column of A is one independent degree of freedom.

**Parameters**

- **first_orbit_ita** (`str`) — Symbolic coordinates of the site, e.g. 'x,y,1/2'.

**Returns**

- **A** (`(3, n_dof) array`) — One column per free parameter, ordered by first appearance in the string (x, y, z within one coordinate); no columns for a fixed site.

**Examples**

'x,y,1/2'  →  representative can move in x and y  →  A is 3×2:

    [[1, 0],
     [0, 1],
     [0, 0]]

'0,0,z'    →  only z is free  →  A is 3×1:

    [[0],
     [0],
     [1]]

'x,x,0'    →  one DoF, but shared between the first two coords  →  A is 3×1:

    [[1],
     [1],
     [0]]

conventional and primitive cells have different multiplicities;
generate_projected_structure tries ``oa`` and then ``omc`` against the actual atoms.

(U+03B1). Both are accepted.

**Parameters**

- **spg_number** (`int`) — International Tables space-group number.
- **letters** (`iterable of str or None`) — Wyckoff letters to extract; None extracts every letter of the selected record.
- **hall_number** (`int or None`) — Passed to load_spacegroup.

**Returns**

- `dict` — ``{letter: {"A": ..., "oa": ..., "omc": ...}}``.

**Raises**

Check whether ``orbit`` reproduces the atom positions in ``idxs``.

Every atom of the orbit is tried as generator and the one with the smallest matching

- **idxs** (`list[int]`) — 1-based atom indices belonging to this orbit.

- **tol** (`float`) — Fractional-coordinate tolerance for position matching.

### `solve_orbit_parameters` { #wyckoff-projector--solve-orbit-parameters }

`solve_orbit_parameters(pos, idxs, oa, tol=1e-06)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 751

Find the site parameters p and the member->atom mapping for the atoms ``idxs``.

Tries every atom of the orbit as member 0 (with the 27 integer shifts that make the
fractional coordinates consistent), solves M_0[:, used] p = x - v_0 in the least-squares
sense, and accepts when the generated orbit is a bijection onto the atoms (match_orbit
within ``tol``).

**Parameters**

- **pos** (`(N, 3) array`) — All fractional positions in the unit cell (0-based).
- **idxs** (`list[int]`) — 1-based atom indices belonging to this orbit.
- **oa** (`(m, 4, 4) array`) — Affine orbit operators of the record (parameter maps, see above).
- **tol** (`float`) — Fractional-coordinate tolerance, for the least-squares residual and for match_orbit.

**Returns**

- `(p, mapping, used) or None` — ``p`` the site parameters, ``mapping[k]`` the 1-based atom index at member k and ``used`` the indices of the free parameters; ``None`` when the operator count differs from ``len(idxs)`` or no atom/shift reproduces the orbit.

### `fit_orbit_parameters` { #wyckoff-projector--fit-orbit-parameters }

`fit_orbit_parameters(disp, mapping, oa, used)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 806

Least-squares fit of ONE parameter increment dp to the raw displacements of all orbit
members: M_k[:, used] dp = u_k.

**Parameters**

- **disp** (`dict[int, (3,) array]`) — Fractional displacements by 1-based atom index (from ``outfile.uc_displacements``).
- **mapping** (`list[int]`) — mapping[k] = 1-based atom index of orbit member k (from solve_orbit_parameters).
- **oa** (`(m, 4, 4) array`) — Affine orbit operators of the record (parameter maps).
- **used** (`list[int]`) — Indices of the free parameters (from solve_orbit_parameters).

**Returns**

- **dp** (`(len(used),) array`) — Fitted parameter increment; empty when the site has no free parameter.
- **U_raw** (`(m, 3) array`) — Raw displacements of the members, fractional.
- **U_fit** (`(m, 3) array`) — Fitted displacements M_k[:, used] dp, fractional; zero when the site has no free parameter.
- **rms** (`float`) — RMS residual of the fit, fractional; the RMS of U_raw when the site has no free parameter.

**Raises**

- `KeyError` — If an atom of ``mapping`` is absent from ``disp``.

### `fit_orbit_displacement_all_atoms` { #wyckoff-projector--fit-orbit-displacement-all-atoms }

`fit_orbit_displacement_all_atoms(disp, mapping, orbit, A)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 854

Fit one shared Wyckoff-DoF parameter vector p for the entire orbit (position-space fit;
generate_projected_structure uses fit_orbit_parameters instead).

**Physical model**

The allowed displacement of atom k in the orbit is:

    u_k  =  R_k  A  p   +  noise

where:

  - R_k  is the 3×3 rotation that maps the representative site to atom k
         (extracted from orbit[k]). Translations do not affect
         displacements, only rotations do.
  - A    is the (3 × n_dof) basis of allowed displacements at the orbit[0] site,
         built by build_A from the coordinate string of orbit member 0.
  - p    is the (n_dof,) vector of Wyckoff DoF parameters — the unknowns.

Stacking all m atoms gives the overdetermined system:

    B  p  ≈  U

with B of shape (3m × n_dof) and U the stacked raw displacements.
The least-squares solution averages out TDEP numerical noise across all
orbit members symmetrically, rather than relying on a single atom.

**Note on coordinate frames**

Everything here is in FRACTIONAL coordinates (both displacements and A).
The orbit rotation matrices R_k are the 3×3 upper-left blocks of the
affine operators, which act on fractional coordinates. No Cartesian
conversion is needed: fractional in, fractional out throughout.

**Parameters**

- **disp** (`dict[int → (3,)]`) — Per-atom fractional displacements from outfile.uc_displacements. Atoms absent from the dict are treated as zero displacement.
- **mapping** (`list[int]`) — mapping[k] = 1-based atom index for orbit operator k. Constructed by build_index_map; mapping[0] is the orbit[0] atom.
- **orbit** (`(m, 4, 4) array`) — Full affine orbit operators (fractional coordinates).
- **A** (`(3, n_dof) array`) — Wyckoff displacement basis at the orbit[0] site.

**Returns**

- **p** (`(n_dof,) array`) — Fitted Wyckoff DoF parameters.
- **urep_proj** (`(3,) array`) — Projected displacement at the orbit[0] site: A @ p.
- **U_raw** (`(m, 3) array`) — Raw displacements from TDEP, one row per orbit member.
- **U_fit** (`(m, 3) array`) — Model displacements R_k @ urep_proj, one row per orbit member.
- **rms** (`float`) — RMS residual |U_raw - U_fit| in fractional units.

### `check_displacement_magnitude` { #wyckoff-projector--check-displacement-magnitude }

`check_displacement_magnitude(lat, pos_old, pos_new, idxs, mapping, orbit, seed_atom, max_disp_angstrom=2.0)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 956

Guardrail 1 (position path): reject unphysically large displacements. Not called by

- **orbit** (`(m, 4, 4) array`) — Affine orbit operators.
- **seed_atom** (`int`) — 1-based index of the orbit[0] atom in the new structure (= mapping[0]).
- **max_disp_angstrom** (`float`) — Abort threshold in Å.

**Raises**

### `generate_projected_structure` { #wyckoff-projector--generate-projected-structure }

`generate_projected_structure(refined_ucposcar_path, displacements_path='outfile.uc_displacements', out_path='outfile.uc_projected_structure', symprec=1e-12, max_disp_angstrom=2.0, min_dist_angstrom=0.3, orbit_tol=1e-05, enforce_input_spacegroup=True, damping=0.8)` — `warpt/Wyckoff_Projector.py`, line 1124

Project TDEP first-order displacements onto Wyckoff site parameters and write the updated
structure.

**Workflow per orbit (atoms grouped by spglib's ``equivalent_atoms``)**

1. solve_orbit_parameters with the ``oa`` operators of the spglib Wyckoff letter, then
   ``omc``; if neither reproduces the atoms, every other record of the group is tried and
   the first that does is used (its letter replaces spglib's).
2. fit_orbit_parameters: one parameter increment dp fitted to the displacements of all
   members (least squares).
3. p_new = p_site - damping * dp; all members regenerated from p_new.
4. Guardrails on the staged positions: check_displacement_magnitude_staged,
   check_atoms_too_close (against all orbits committed so far) and, if
   ``enforce_input_spacegroup``, check_spacegroup_preserved.
5. The orbit is committed.

**Parameters**

- **refined_ucposcar_path** (`str`) — VASP5 unit cell to update (``infile.ucposcar`` in a WARP step).
- **displacements_path** (`str`) — TDEP ``outfile.uc_displacements``: one line per atom, ``index dx dy dz``, fractional; blank lines, ``#`` lines and lines without exactly four fields are skipped.
- **out_path** (`str`) — Where the projected structure is written (VASP5, scale 1.0, Direct).
- **symprec** (`float`) — spglib symmetry tolerance in Å (default 1e-12; `warpt.tdep_extract_fc.run_extract_fc` passes 1e-5).
- **max_disp_angstrom** (`float`) — Abort if any atom moves more than this, in Å (default 2.0).
- **min_dist_angstrom** (`float`) — Abort if any atom pair comes closer than this, in Å (default 0.3). In a WARP step the committed structure is checked again, with 0.5 Å, by `warpt.tdep_extract_fc.assert_structure_physical`.
- **orbit_tol** (`float`) — Fractional-coordinate tolerance for orbit matching (default 1e-5).
- **enforce_input_spacegroup** (`bool`) — Run guardrail 3 (default True).
- **damping** (`float`) — Fraction of the fitted parameter increment applied (default 0.8).

**Returns**

- **out_path** (`str`) — The path the projected structure was written to.
- **rep_info** (`list[dict]`) — One dict per orbit: eqid, letter, seed_atom (mapping[0]), site_parameters, free_parameters, members, mapping, fit_rms_fractional, rep_displacement_projected (fitted displacement of member 0) and fit_parameters (dp).

**Side effects**

Writes ``out_path``; prints the per-orbit report to stdout.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — If spglib cannot identify the symmetry, if an orbit is reproduced by no record of the group, or if a guardrail trips (message prefixed ``[guardrail:...]``).
- `KeyError` — If a Wyckoff letter is absent from the table record, or if an atom of an orbit has no line in ``displacements_path``.

## warpt.context_state

### class `WarpContext` { #context-state--warpcontext }

`WarpContext(root: str, master_scf: str, ucp: str, awk_cmd: str, pwscf_run: str, temp: int, num_samples: int, quantum: bool, cutoffFC2: float, cutoffFC3: Optional[float], supercell: Sequence[str], sc_opts: Sequence[str], metric: str, reuse_threshold: float, max_freq: Optional[int], T_debye: Optional[int], sigma_mode: str, sigma_ext: np.ndarray, press_conv_th: float, kB_eV: float, hbar_eVs: float, EV_TO_GPA_A3: float, precond_schedule: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None, wyckoff_damping: float = 0.8, firstorder_min_freq: float = -1.0, fc1_mean_tol: float = 0.03, fc1_max_tol: float = 0.075, lattice_damping: float = 1.0, elastic_constants: Optional[str] = None, lattice_damping_ladder: Optional[str] = None, lattice_noise_z0: float = 0.0, press_conv_noise_k: float = 0.0, fc3_gate_thr: Optional[float] = None, fc3_gate_max_retries: int = 2, fc3_gate_nscale: float = 1.0, wz_supercell: Optional[str] = None, masses: Optional[dict] = None)` — `warpt/context_state.py`, line 24

Immutable run configuration shared by every pipeline stage.

Paths: ``root`` (run root, the launch directory), ``master_scf``, ``ucp``.
Calculator: ``pwscf_run`` (command that runs one SCF or MLIP evaluation),
``awk_cmd`` (``mawk`` or ``awk``).
Sampling: ``temp`` (K), ``num_samples``, ``quantum``, ``masses`` (per-element masses
in amu, None = natural), and for the geom_0 bootstrap ``max_freq`` (THz) and
``T_debye`` (K).
Force constants: ``cutoffFC2`` and ``cutoffFC3`` (Å; ``None`` = no third order),
``wz_supercell``.
Supercell: ``supercell`` (raw CLI strings), ``sc_opts`` (generate_structure flags).
Position loop: ``metric``, ``reuse_threshold``, ``fc1_mean_tol`` and
``fc1_max_tol`` (eV/Å), ``wyckoff_damping``.
Lattice step: ``sigma_mode``, ``sigma_ext`` (GPa, tension positive, Voigt),
``press_conv_th`` (GPa), ``lattice_damping``, ``elastic_constants``, ``lattice_damping_ladder``,
``lattice_noise_z0``, ``press_conv_noise_k``, ``fc3_gate_thr`` (GPa),
``fc3_gate_max_retries``, ``fc3_gate_nscale``.
Constants: ``kB_eV``, ``hbar_eVs``, ``EV_TO_GPA_A3``.
Preconditioning: ``precond_schedule`` overrides the sample schedule and
``firstorder_min_freq`` (THz) gates the first-order structure update from geom_2 on.

### class `WarpState` { #context-state--warpstate }

`WarpState(current_dir: str, lattice_changed: bool = False, last_update_significant: bool = False, last_sigma_int: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, resume_vc_dir: Optional[str] = None, use_fake_fc: bool = False, fc3_gate_events: list = field(default_factory=list))` — `warpt/context_state.py`, line 138

Mutable run-time state carried across a vc-relax.

``current_dir``: directory of the stage being executed. ``lattice_changed``:
set after a lattice update and cleared by the next position step, which then
samples fresh instead of merging the previous samples.
``last_update_significant``: the most recent position step moved the
structure by more than ``reuse_threshold``, which blocks sample merging in
the following step. ``use_fake_fc``: sample from TDEP's fake force constants
(geom_0 only). ``fc3_gate_events``: one ``(iteration, attempt, n_samples,
mismatch GPa)`` tuple per FC3-gate evaluation. ``last_sigma_int`` and
``resume_vc_dir`` are declared but not written or read by any stage.
`warpt.workflow_vc_relax.run_vc_relax` also attaches
``last_lattice_rel_change`` and ``prev_sigma_ph`` at run time.

## warpt.resume

### `complete_dir` { #resume--complete-dir }

`complete_dir(ctx, state, *, expected_ns, extract_mode, want_dos=False, want_gruneisen=False, want_lattice=False, want_ifc=True, on_collect=None, run_phonons=None, run_lattice=None)` — `warpt/resume.py`, line 45

- **expected_ns** (`int`) — Number of configurations this step should have.
- **extract_mode** (`str`) — ``"second"``, ``"second_third"`` or ``"second_third_first"`` for `warpt.tdep_extract_fc.run_extract_fc`.
- **want_dos, want_gruneisen, want_lattice, want_ifc** (`bool`) — Forwarded to `warpt.validity.first_missing_stage` to define which optional stages this directory needs.
- **on_collect** (`callable or None`) — Run immediately after ``collect_stats`` so a resume that redoes collect also redoes the caller's sample combination.
- **run_phonons** (`callable or None`) — Produces the phonon output required by ``want_dos`` (``outfile.dispersion_relations.hdf5``) or ``want_gruneisen`` (``outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5`` with Grüneisen data). The only producer of that grid file, `warpt.phonon_stress.internal_stress_voigt`, removes it after extracting ``sigma_ph``, so ``valid_gruneisen`` then fails and a ``want_gruneisen`` directory cannot complete: the 16-action guard exits via ``die``.
- **run_lattice** (`callable or None`) — Produces ``outfile.new_vc_ucposcar``.

**Returns**

- `int` — Number of stage actions executed; 0 when the directory was already complete.

**Side effects**

Whatever the stage functions write in the working directory; ``ifc_pressure``
is launched as a shell command; ``extract_forceconstants`` runs with
``OMP_NUM_THREADS=1``.

**Raises**

Calls `warpt.utilities.die` (exit 1) when the setup files are missing,
a needed callback is absent, ``ifc_pressure`` fails, a stage does not advance
within 16 actions, or an unknown stage name is returned. Errors raised by the
stage functions propagate: ``SystemExit`` via ``die`` from sampling, collect
and extraction, ``RuntimeError`` from
`warpt.runner.run_jobs_parallel` when a job's output lacks
``JOB DONE.``.

### `find_resume_plan` { #restart-check--find-resume-plan }

`find_resume_plan(ctx) -> dict` — `warpt/restart_check.py`, line 53

Locate where an interrupted run should continue.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — Run configuration; ``ctx.root`` and ``ctx.master_scf`` are used.

**Returns**

- `dict` — ``iter``: iteration to continue: 0 when no ``iter_*`` exists, the last index when a checked directory of the last iteration reports a missing stage, last index + 1 otherwise (on the normal path only when the last iteration has neither a ``lattice_`` nor a ``position_*`` directory, since both report a missing stage even when finished, see below); ``dir``: directory to continue in, or ``None``; ``stage``: its first missing stage, or ``None``; ``kind``: ``"lattice"``, ``"position"``, ``"preconditioning"`` or ``"none"``. Checks, in order, ``lattice_`` with ``want_gruneisen`` and ``want_lattice`` set (a finished lattice step is reported at stage ``"phonons"`` because ``outfile.grid_dispersions.hdf5`` is removed by `warpt.phonon_stress.internal_stress_voigt`), ``position_*`` newest first with the default ``want_ifc=True`` (a finished position step is reported at stage ``"ifc_pressure"`` because position steps never run ``ifc_pressure``), then ``preconditioning/geom_*`` newest first (DOS stage required). The plan is printed only; ``run_vc_relax`` resumes by its own forward walk.

**Side effects**

Changes into each inspected directory and restores the original working
directory before returning.

whenever ``rotational_average_order`` is not None, including 0, and its

Evaluate one structure with the MLIP and print the QE-like block to stdout.

**Parameters**

- **args** (`argparse.Namespace`) — Parsed options of `main`; ``args.input`` is used when ``input_path`` is None and ``args.allow_no_stress`` selects zero stress when none is available.
- **calc** (`ase.calculators.calculator.Calculator or None`) — Calculator to reuse; built with `make_calc` when None.
- **input_path** (`str or None`) — QE input file to read instead of ``args.input``.

**Side effects**

Prints the QE-like block to stdout (`warpt.io_qe.print_qe_like`): the
energy in Ry, the forces in Ry/bohr (sign preserved) and the stress in Ry/bohr³
with the sign flipped to QE's compression-positive convention. Returns None.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — When the calculator provides no stress and ``--allow_no_stress`` is not set.

### `run_batch` { #mlip-interface--run-batch }

`run_batch(args)` — `warpt/MLIP_interface.py`, line 269

Evaluate every structure of ``args.batch`` in this process with one calculator.

The batch file lists ``<input> <output>`` pairs, one per line; blank lines and
lines starting with ``#`` are ignored. The calculator is built once and reused,
so the freshness of the results relies on `_rot_avg_order` (no
``SymmetrizedCalculator`` wrapper) and on `run_once` requesting forces before
the energy.

**Side effects**

For each pair, stdout is redirected to the output file, which receives the
QE-like block followed by ``JOB DONE.``, or ``JOB FAILED. <error>`` when the
evaluation raises (the error is also printed to stderr). Finished outputs stay
valid if a later structure fails, so the runner's resume logic can reuse them.
Returns None; calls ``sys.exit(1)`` after the loop if any structure failed.

### `main` { #mlip-interface--main }

`main()` — `warpt/MLIP_interface.py`, line 319

Command-line entry point.

Options: ``-input`` (QE input; required unless ``--batch``), ``--batch`` (list of
``<input> <output>`` pairs), ``--engine`` (``upet``, the default, or ``mace``),
``--device`` (``cpu``, the default, or ``cuda``), ``--ml_params`` (model file),
``--model`` (UPET model name, default ``pet-mad-s``, one of the ``MODELS`` keys),
``--version`` (UPET model version; default: the ``MODELS`` entry for ``--model``,
else ``latest``), ``--conservative``, ``--variant``, ``--rot-avg``,
``--rot-avg-batch``, ``--dispersion``, ``--dtype`` and ``--allow_no_stress``.

Single mode prints the QE-like block and ``JOB DONE.`` to stdout, or
``JOB FAILED. <error>`` and exits 1. Batch mode writes one output file per
structure and prints ``JOB DONE.`` to its own stdout when every structure
succeeded, else exits 1.

Pressure, stress anisotropy, residual forces and cell parameters of ``atoms``.

### `main` { #upet-relax--main }

`main()` — `warpt/upet_relax.py`, line 153

Command-line entry point; returns the process exit code (0, 1 or 3).

Parses the options, loads the checkpoint, reports the starting state, relaxes the
cell and positions with ``FrechetCellFilter`` under ``FixSymmetry`` (unless
``--no-fixsym``), evaluates and prints the gate (optimizer converged, |P - target|,
anisotropy, symmetrised residual force, space group unchanged), then writes the
POSCAR and the optional JSON report (which records the gate result) and returns 3
when the gate failed.

Options without a help text: ``--device`` (torch device, ``cpu`` (default) or
``cuda``), ``--steps`` (maximum number of optimizer steps, default 500),
``--optimizer`` (``lbfgs`` (default) or ``fire``) and ``--symprec`` (symmetry
tolerance in Å for spglib and FixSymmetry, default 1e-5).

## warpt.io_qe

### `read_qe_input_file` { #io-qe--read-qe-input-file }

`read_qe_input_file(filename: str)` — `warpt/io_qe.py`, line 33

Read a Quantum ESPRESSO ``pw.x`` input file.

**Parameters**

- **filename** (`str`) — Path to the input file.

**Returns**

- `ase.Atoms` — The structure, as returned by ``ase.io.espresso.read_espresso_in``, atoms in file order.

### `print_qe_like` { #io-qe--print-qe-like }

`print_qe_like(atoms, energy_ry, forces_ry_bohr, stress_ry_bohr3, source='MLIP_interface')` — `warpt/io_qe.py`, line 51

Print energy, forces and stress in a minimal QE-like format.

Emits the lines the WARP collector parses (atom count; total energy on a ``!``
line; per-atom ``force =`` lines; the ``total stress (Ry/bohr**3)`` block, each row
followed by its kbar values) together with QE-style header lines (title, forces
header, stress header with ``P=`` in kbar). The caller prints ``JOB DONE.``
afterwards. No other line may contain ``!``: the collector takes the energy from
the last line that does.

**Parameters**

- **atoms** (`ase.Atoms`) — The structure.
- **energy_ry** (`float`) — Total energy in Ry.
- **forces_ry_bohr** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (N, 3)`) — Forces in Ry/bohr (force-on-atom sign).
- **stress_ry_bohr3** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)`) — Stress in Ry/bohr³, compression-positive (QE convention).
- **source** (`str`) — Backend named on the title line (default ``MLIP_interface``).

### `read_qe_stress_gpa` { #io-qe--read-qe-stress-gpa }

`read_qe_stress_gpa(qe_out_path: str, rybohr3_to_gpa: float, kbar_to_gpa: float = 0.1) -> np.ndarray` — `warpt/io_qe.py`, line 94

Return the 3x3 total stress in GPa from a Quantum ESPRESSO-style output file.

Finds the first line containing ``total stress`` (any whitespace between the words,
case-insensitive) and reads the next three lines. If the header mentions ``Ry/bohr`` (the QE
header does) or mentions neither unit, the first three numbers of each row are multiplied
by ``rybohr3_to_gpa``; if it mentions only ``kbar`` they are multiplied by ``kbar_to_gpa``.

**Parameters**

- **qe_out_path** (`str`) — Output file to parse: a ``pw.x`` output or the block printed by `warpt.MLIP_interface` or `warpt.VASP_interface`.
- **rybohr3_to_gpa** (`float`) — Ry/bohr³ to GPa (``warpt.constants.RYBOHR3_TO_GPA``).
- **kbar_to_gpa** (`float`) — kbar to GPa (default 0.1).

**Returns**

- `numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)` — Stress in GPa, sign as printed (compression-positive).

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — If no header is found, if fewer than three lines follow it, or if a row has fewer than three fields.
- `ValueError` — If one of the first three fields of a row is not a number.

`prepare_infiles_from_uc(src_uc: str, sc_opts: Sequence[str]) -> None` — `warpt/io_workflow.py`, line 57

Create the TDEP structure infiles in the current directory from a unit-cell POSCAR.

Copies ``src_uc`` to ``infile.ucposcar``, runs ``generate_structure`` with ``sc_opts`` (the
flags from `warpt.utilities.parse_supercell`) and copies ``outfile.ssposcar`` to
``infile.ssposcar``. Exits via ``die`` if ``generate_structure`` fails or writes no
``outfile.ssposcar``.

### `copy_previous` { #io-workflow--copy-previous }

`copy_previous(prev_dir: str, sc_opts: Sequence[str]) -> None` — `warpt/io_workflow.py`, line 74

Hand geometry and force constants over from ``prev_dir`` to the current directory.

Rebuilds ``infile.ucposcar`` and ``infile.ssposcar`` from the best unit cell of ``prev_dir``
(`latest_uc`, then `prepare_infiles_from_uc`). If ``infile.forceconstant`` is
absent from the current directory, ``prev_dir/outfile.forceconstant`` is copied to it; the
run exits via ``die`` when that file is missing.
``prev_dir/outfile.forceconstant_thirdorder`` is copied to
``infile.forceconstant_thirdorder`` when it exists and the target does not.

### `write_isotopes` { #io-workflow--write-isotopes }

`write_isotopes(masses: dict, poscar: str = 'infile.ucposcar', out: str = 'infile.isotopes') -> str` — `warpt/io_workflow.py`, line 104

Write TDEP's ``infile.isotopes`` for the atoms of ``poscar`` with the masses in ``masses``.

The file has, for every atom in the order of ``poscar``, a line with the number of isotopes
(always 1 here) followed by one line ``concentration mass``. Elements absent from
``masses`` (``{symbol: mass in amu}``) get their standard atomic weight (ASE). TDEP reads
the file when ``--readiso`` is passed to ``canonical_configuration`` or
``phonon_dispersion_relations``. Returns ``out``.

## warpt.tensors

### `to_voigt` { #tensors--to-voigt }

`to_voigt(mat: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` — `warpt/tensors.py`, line 30

Contract a symmetric 3x3 tensor to its 6-component Voigt vector.

Off-diagonals are symmetrised but **not** doubled, i.e. the result is the
stress-style Voigt vector ``[xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy]``.

**Parameters**

- **mat** (`numpy.ndarray`) — Array with trailing shape ``(3, 3)`` (broadcasting over leading axes is supported).

**Returns**

- `numpy.ndarray` — Array with the trailing ``(3, 3)`` replaced by a length-6 Voigt axis.

### `voigt_to_strain` { #tensors--voigt-to-strain }

`voigt_to_strain(voigt: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` — `warpt/tensors.py`, line 58

Expand a Voigt strain vector to the symmetric 3x3 strain tensor.

The input is interpreted as *engineering* strain (components 4-6 are
``2*eps_ij``), so the shear entries are halved on the way back to the
tensor form.

**Parameters**

- **voigt** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6,)`) — Engineering strain in Voigt order ``[xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy]``.

**Returns**

- `numpy.ndarray, shape (3, 3)` — The symmetric tensor strain.

### `voigt_trace` { #tensors--voigt-trace }

`voigt_trace(sig6: np.ndarray) -> float` — `warpt/tensors.py`, line 83

Tensor trace of a Voigt vector, i.e. ``xx + yy + zz``.

**Parameters**

- **sig6** (`numpy.ndarray, shape (6,)`) — A Voigt vector (stress or strain).

**Returns**

- `float` — The sum of the three normal components.

Return the name of the first incomplete stage in the current directory.

Walks the pipeline in order (setup -> sampling -> scf -> collect -> extract
-> ifc_pressure -> phonons -> lattice) and returns the first stage whose
validity check fails, or ``None`` if everything required is present. The
``want_*`` flags select which optional stages this particular step requires:
`warpt.workflow_vc_relax.run_vc_relax` checks a position step with
``want_ifc=False`` and ``want_lattice=False``, whereas
`warpt.restart_check.find_resume_plan` leaves ``want_ifc`` at its default
and therefore reports a finished position step at stage ``ifc_pressure``.

**Parameters**

- **ctx** (`context_state.WarpContext`) — Run context; only ``ctx.master_scf`` is used here.
- **want_dos, want_gruneisen, want_lattice** (`bool`) — Require the DOS-phonon, Grüneisen-grid, and lattice-update stages.
- **want_ifc** (`bool`) — Require ``ifc_pressure`` output (true for preconditioning/lattice steps, false for pure position steps).
- **expected_ns** (`int or None`) — Expected number of sampled configurations, if known.

**Returns**

- `str or None` — The first missing stage name, or ``None`` if complete.

comment line (see `spacegroups`). Unless ``quiet``, prints one table line per frame

## warpt.trajectory

### `read_poscar` { #trajectory--read-poscar }

`read_poscar(path)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 72

Read the POSCAR file at ``path`` with ASE (format ``vasp``) and return an ``ase.Atoms``.

Distinct from `warpt.io_poscar.read_poscar` (lattice and raw lines) and
`warpt.structconv.read_poscar` (text to ``Structure``). A path containing ``@`` is
opened as a file handle because ASE parses ``name@index`` as slice syntax. Errors from
``ase.io.read`` (missing or malformed file) propagate.

### `step_dirs` { #trajectory--step-dirs }

`step_dirs(root)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 87

Every step directory of the run, in the order WARP visits them.

Only directories named exactly ``iter_<N>`` are read; sidelined copies such as
``iter_6.stale`` are ignored (`warpt.get_frames.stage_dirs` includes them).
Within an iteration: ``preconditioning/geom_*``, then
``position_*``, then ``lattice_``. Returns a list of ``(iter, kind, index, path)`` with
``kind`` in ``precond``, ``position``, ``lattice``.

### `step_dirs._n` { #trajectory--step-dirs--n }

`_n(p)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 97

Iteration number of a directory named exactly ``iter_<N>``, else None.

### `symmetry` { #trajectory--symmetry }

`symmetry(atoms)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 116

Highest space-group number found over SYMPREC_LADDER, and the tightest symprec (Å) at
which that number is still found.

The tightest symprec falls as a structure settles onto a higher-symmetry parent, so it
measures how well the symmetry is satisfied without naming a target group. Returns
``(None, None)`` without spglib or when every symprec fails.

### `spacegroup_at` { #trajectory--spacegroup-at }

`spacegroup_at(atoms, symprec)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 144

Space-group number at one symprec (Å), or None without spglib or on failure.

### `site_symmetry` { #trajectory--site-symmetry }

`site_symmetry(atoms)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 156

Space group and the Wyckoff site of every atom, at SYMPREC_REF.

Returns ``(number, symbol, sites)``: the space-group number, its Hermann-Mauguin symbol
(spglib's, e.g. ``P2_1/m``) and, per atom in file order, the site of its orbit as element,
multiplicity and Wyckoff letter, e.g. ``H32f``; a site shared by several orbits gets ``-2``,
``-3``, ... on its later orbits. The multiplicity is that of the conventional cell (the
number of the orbit's atoms in spglib's standardised cell), so it is the tabulated one also
when the run uses a primitive cell or a supercell. ``(None, None, [])`` without spglib or
when spglib fails.

### `orbit_sites` { #trajectory--orbit-sites }

`orbit_sites(atoms)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 198

One representative atom per symmetry orbit and the Wyckoff site it occupies.

Returns a list of ``(index, site)``, ``index`` the 0-based position of the first atom of the
orbit in ``atoms`` and ``site`` as in `site_symmetry`. Empty without spglib or when
spglib fails.

### `fc1` { #trajectory--fc1 }

`fc1(path)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 213

``(mean, max)`` residual force in eV/Å from ``path/outfile.forceconstant_firstorder``
(workflow_vc_relax.fc1_stats, run inside ``path``); ``(0.0, 0.0)`` when the file is absent
or has no data rows (fc1_stats); ``(None, None)`` on any error.

### `min_freq` { #trajectory--min-freq }

`min_freq(path)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 229

Minimum frequency (THz) over all bands in ``path/outfile.dispersion_relations``, or None.

### `voigt` { #trajectory--voigt }

`voigt(path, name)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 240

First six numbers of ``path/name`` as a Voigt vector, skipping ``#`` lines; None if the
file is absent, unparsable or holds fewer than six numbers.

### `stresses` { #trajectory--stresses }

`stresses(path)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 257

Internal stress of a lattice step in WARP's tension-positive convention.

Returns ``{sigma0, sigma_ph, sigma_int}`` (Voigt, GPa) or None when any of
``outfile.stress_dft/fc2/fc3`` is missing. ``sigma0 = -(dft + fc2 + fc3)`` because those
files are compression-positive; ``outfile.sigma_ph`` is written by workflow_vc_relax
already tension-positive and is added without negation. ``sigma_ph`` and ``sigma_int`` are
None when ``outfile.sigma_ph`` is absent.

### `voigt_to_matrix` { #trajectory--voigt-to-matrix }

`voigt_to_matrix(v)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 280

Voigt (xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy) -> 3x3.

### `cartesian_ops` { #trajectory--cartesian-ops }

`cartesian_ops(atoms, symprec=1e-05)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 287

The crystal's point operations as Cartesian (3, 3) matrices.

spglib returns rotations acting on FRACTIONAL column vectors. With lattice
vectors as ROWS of L, a Cartesian row vector transforms as r' = r L^-1 R^T L,
so the operation acting on column vectors is O = (L^-1 R^T L)^T -- which is
what a rank-2 tensor needs.

**Parameters**

atoms : ase.Atoms
- **symprec** (`float`) — spglib tolerance in Å (default 1e-5).

**Returns**

- `list of (3, 3) arrays, or None` — None without spglib or when spglib cannot identify the symmetry.

### `forbidden_stress` { #trajectory--forbidden-stress }

`forbidden_stress(sigma_voigt, ops)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 325

Largest symmetry-forbidden component of a stress tensor, in GPa.

A stress must satisfy sigma = O sigma O^T for every point operation O, so the group
average is the projection onto the allowed subspace and ``max|sigma - average|`` is the
forbidden part. Works for any space group without case analysis.

``ops`` must come from a fixed reference structure, not from the step being tested:
recomputed per step, a drifting cell loses operations, the average is taken over the
reduced group and the forbidden part shrinks exactly when the structure is losing symmetry.

**Parameters**

- **sigma_voigt** (`array (6,)`) — Stress in Voigt order, GPa.
- **ops** (`list of (3, 3) arrays`) — Cartesian point operations from cartesian_ops.

**Returns**

- `float or None` — None when ``ops`` is empty or ``sigma_voigt`` is None.

### `nconfigs` { #trajectory--nconfigs }

`nconfigs(path)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 358

Number of lines in ``path/infile.stat`` (one per sampled configuration), or None.

### `press_ext` { #trajectory--press-ext }

`press_ext(root)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 367

Target pressure in GPa, or None.

Searches, in order, ``warpt_run.log`` (``press_ext=<value>`` or ``press_ext <value>``),
``run_warpt.sh``, ``run.sh`` and ``job*`` (``--press_ext
<value>``) in ``root``; as a last resort the absolute value of the first component of the last
``σ_ext: [...]`` line of the stress diagnostic block in ``warpt_run.log``.

Only the first number is read, so for a three- or six-component ``--press_ext`` the result
is the xx component. The patterns match unsigned numbers only and the ``σ_ext`` fallback
takes the absolute value, so the result is always a compressive (positive) pressure; a
tensile target is not recovered with its sign.

### `harvest` { #trajectory--harvest }

`harvest(root, pext=None)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 401

Collect one row of metrics per step directory under ``root``.

Returns ``(rows, pext)``: ``rows`` is a list of dicts (the coordinate columns are
``w_<atom>_x/y/z`` and ``site_<atom>``, e.g. ``w_H4_z``), ``pext`` the target pressure from
``pext`` when given, else from press_ext, or None. Steps without a readable ``infile.ucposcar`` are skipped;
``press_resid_GPa`` (``max|sigma_int - sigma_ext|`` against the hydrostatic target
``[-pext, -pext, -pext, 0, 0, 0]``) needs ``pext``, and ``dsigma_ph_GPa`` a previous step
with ``outfile.sigma_ph``.

`_site_text(site)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 509

``H18h`` -> ``("H", "18h")``, ``H6c-2`` -> ``("H", "6c(2)")``; ``(site, "")`` otherwise.

### `active_dofs` { #trajectory--active-dofs }

`active_dofs(rows, n_max=3, tol=1e-06)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 552

The atomic coordinates that move, most active first.

A coordinate pinned by site symmetry stays constant; a free one varies. Values are
unwrapped across 0/1 step by step (`unwrap`) before the span is taken.

**Returns**

- **keys** (`list[str]`) — Up to ``n_max`` column names (``w_<atom>_<xyz>``) with span above ``tol``, largest span first.
- **span** (`dict`) — Span (max - min, fractional) of every moving coordinate.

### `show_file` { #trajectory--show-file }

`show_file(path)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 594

Open ``path`` in the OS viewer (``open``, ``xdg-open`` or ``start``); failures are

### `plot` { #trajectory--plot }

`plot(rows, out, dofs=(), show=False)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 609

Draw the six-panel figure of the cell and the free coordinates, and save it to ``out``.

Left column: the lattice parameters a, b and c (Å), each on its own axis so that small
changes stay visible. Right column: the cell angles alpha, beta and gamma (degrees) on one
axis, the volume per atom (Å³), and the ``dofs`` atomic coordinates relative to the first
step. Every lattice step is marked by a vertical line, and the title gives the space group
at the first and at the last step. Saved as PNG at 150 dpi; with ``show`` the file is also
opened via show_file. Skipped with a message when matplotlib is unavailable.

**Parameters**

- **rows** (`list of dict`) — Output of `harvest`.
- **out** (`str`) — Path of the PNG to write.
- **dofs** (`sequence of str`) — Coordinate columns to plot (``w_<atom>_<x|y|z>``), from `active_dofs`.
- **show** (`bool`) — Open the written file in a viewer.

### `plot.col` { #trajectory--plot-col }

`col(k)` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 641

Column ``k`` of ``rows`` as a float array, NaN where the value is missing.

### `main` { #trajectory--main }

`main()` — `warpt/trajectory.py`, line 723

Command-line entry point: harvest ``run_dir`` (the run root), write the CSV, print the
summary and, unless ``--no-plot``, draw the figure. Exits with a message when no step is
found.
